requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 and node2
requirements.summary: useradd -m plus passwd -l succeeded on both nodes; id opsbot confirms uid=1000(opsbot) exists on node1 and node2, and the account persisted through the post-task reboot of both nodes.

requirements.requirement: Give opsbot on node1 SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: An ed25519 keypair was generated for opsbot on node1 and its public key installed in node2's opsbot authorized_keys. A direct SSH from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 using the key (BatchMode=yes, no password) successfully ran whoami/hostname returning opsbot/node2, and this was re-verified after both nodes were rebooted.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems (i.e. password authentication must not work for opsbot on either node)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed PasswordAuthentication already 'no' globally on both nodes, and an identical Match User opsbot block (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) was added and validated with 'sshd -t' on both node1 and node2, then confirmed still present after both reboots. However, every actual password-only login attempt captured in the trace (cmd-fbdbf028c15c4ca8, cmd-a8648262f74d4ff6, cmd-cb27ae07e2464ca6) targets opsbot@10.100.68.11, i.e. node2's opsbot account, from both node1 and node2 as the source. No command in the trace attempts a password login directly against node1's opsbot account, so enforcement on node1 rests on configuration/syntax validation rather than an observed rejected login, while node2's enforcement is directly demonstrated (including post-restart).

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (node1, node2)
requirements.summary: For node1: pre-restart boot_id (bdd5de93...) and health captured, reboot acknowledged (stream closed as expected), connection reset observed during the transition, post-restart boot_id changed (eee6b2ad...), and opsbot account/keys/outbound SSH to node2 reverified working. For node2: pre-restart boot_id (dfeb3b70...), reboot ack, connection reset, post-restart boot_id changed (dc9b465e...), and opsbot account/authorized_keys plus inbound SSH from node1 reverified working. Fixed lifecycle snapshots independently confirm both boot_id transitions (before_prepare bdd5de93->after_executor eee6b2ad for node1; before_prepare dfeb3b70->after_executor dc9b465e for node2), and show no failed services or package-health issues post-restart.

overall_summary: The opsbot account was created on both nodes and node1's opsbot can authenticate to and run commands on node2's opsbot via ed25519 SSH key, verified both before and after a full restart of each node with matching boot_id transitions. Key-only enforcement (Match User opsbot with AuthenticationMethods publickey) was deployed, syntax-validated, and confirmed to persist across restarts on both nodes, and a rejected-password-login was directly demonstrated against node2's opsbot account both before and after its restart. The one gap is that no command in the trace performs an actual password-login attempt against node1's own opsbot account — enforcement there is supported by identical configuration and passing 'sshd -t', but not by a directly observed rejected login, so that specific outcome is only partially confirmed. Operational hygiene is good: the only mutations beyond the core task (host-key generation, /run/sshd creation, socket restart) were necessary prerequisites for the sshd config to take effect, with no unreverted or unrelated changes.
limitations: No command in the captured trace attempts a password-only login directly against node1's opsbot account; the rejection is inferred from identical Match-block configuration and passing sshd -t rather than an observed failed login on node1 itself.

Reboot acknowledgements returned -1/'exec stream closed' and a subsequent connection-reset error, which is the expected behavior for an in-flight reboot disconnect rather than a task failure, but the transcript does not include a live disruption-window health probe beyond these connection errors.

operational_hygiene.summary: The only state-changing commands beyond the core account/key/sshd-config work were ssh-keygen -A (generating missing host keys) and mkdir /run/sshd — both were necessary prerequisites discovered while validating sshd config with 'sshd -t' (host keys and the privilege-separation directory were absent on this image), not troubleshooting experiments unrelated to the task. systemctl restart ssh.socket was needed to activate the socket-activated sshd with the new host keys and config. One diagnostic SSH attempt from opsbot@node1 to itself (cmd-852039286ba64aff) failed with Permission denied but was read-only and caused no state change. Fixed lifecycle snapshots show only expected boot-id-tied /tmp and socket churn from the reboots, no residual failed services, and consistent dpkg package health before and after. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
